one_liner: Pydantic AI thinks, Kestra schedules, Temporal clocks, Orca reasons, launchd serves. LangChain for graphs, Flowise for visuals. Default to Pydantic AI. Always.

rules.rule: Every new agent, automation, or process starts with Pydantic AI: typed inputs, validated outputs, dependency injection, testable.
rules.d85_note: Typed schemas make MODEL ops validatable; typing does not make them CODE. The four ratios still apply.

rules.rule: LangChain/LangGraph only for complex multi-agent graphs with backtracking, LangSmith enterprise tracing, or Deep Agents context compression.
rules.d85_note: Provider switching alone is NOT a trigger — Pydantic AI is multi-provider. A simple chain in LangChain is overengineering.

rules.rule: Flowise only when a non-engineer must build/modify the agent, or for rapid visual prototyping or client demos.
rules.d85_note: Flowise output is not closed-grammar Python source under an authority root: it cannot pass D85 inventory and is NEVER admissible as a durable system.

rules.rule: Kestra runs the schedule; Pydantic AI runs the logic. Trigger -> Shell task -> Python -> Pydantic AI agent -> structured result -> store/alert.
rules.d85_note: Orchestration is control plane and must be CODE in the flow definition.

rules.rule: Temporal only for durable workflows with a tight start-latency SLA and mandatory catch-up recovery after downtime. If 'around 8am' is fine, use Kestra. Temporal buys durable-execution semantics, not a wall-clock promise.
rules.d85_note: The discriminator is a measured SLA plus recovery policy, nothing else. Schedules can still be delayed by worker availability; admission requires deployment evidence meeting the declared SLA.

rules.rule: Orca only for jobs that need an agent to reason, interpret, or decide. Scripts go to Kestra; agents go to Orca with Pydantic AI I/O.
rules.d85_note: Choosing Orca declares MODEL ops: each requires a D85 necessity record at admission.

property_definitions.claim_semantics: A property is claimed by supplying an evidence record over exactly its schema fields; CODE derives the boolean from the record. A well-formed record whose evidence fails its acceptance predicate is a CONTRADICTED claim and BLOCKS — it is never silently read as FALSE. An absent property is not claimed and is FALSE. No bare booleans are accepted anywhere.

clock_critical.definition: The job carries a written start-latency SLA of at most 60 seconds AND a mandatory catch-up recovery policy: after a crash or missed window the execution must be recovered and delivered late, never skipped. Temporal is selected for durable-execution semantics, not as a wall-clock guarantee — schedules can still be delayed by worker availability, so admission requires deployment evidence meeting the declared SLA.
clock_critical.binary_test: Is there a named consumer that fails if start latency exceeds the SLA, and is skipping after downtime unacceptable?
clock_critical.measurement: Write the SLA number and the recovery policy; name the consumer and the failure mode. If no consumer or failure mode can be named, the property is FALSE.
clock_critical.true_example: Market-open data pull with p95 start latency <= 15s of 09:30:00 ET and mandatory catch-up after downtime.
clock_critical.false_example: Daily 8am digest email — 'by 8:15' is fine, and a missed run can rerun whenever.

evidence_schema.named_consumer: string, non-empty — who breaks when the SLA is missed
evidence_schema.sla_start_latency_seconds: integer 1..60 — the accepted predicate; outside this range the claim is CONTRADICTED (a looser SLA is an ordinary Kestra schedule)
evidence_schema.recovery_policy: 'catch_up' — 'skip' is CONTRADICTED (skip-on-miss is an ordinary schedule)

resident_service.definition: The job must hold a long-lived local resource: a listening socket, a watched directory, a hardware connection, or sub-second response to OS events (file/watchdog/USB). KeepAlive in a plist proves restart policy, not a held resource; it is never sufficient evidence on its own.
resident_service.binary_test: Does the job wait for events rather than being invoked on a schedule?
resident_service.measurement: If the job can be expressed as cron/interval + run-to-completion, the property is FALSE regardless of how it is currently deployed. Corroborating a resident requires source evidence of the resource itself: plist Sockets/WatchPaths/WatchDevices, or an OS-observed listening socket (lsof) — not KeepAlive.
resident_service.true_example: Watchdog daemon monitoring a folder and reacting within 500ms.
resident_service.false_example: Health check that runs every minute — that is a schedule.

evidence_schema.resource_kind: one of listening_socket | watched_directory | hardware_connection | os_event_sub_second
evidence_schema.resource_detail: string, non-empty — the concrete resource held

non_engineer_surface.definition: The primary builder or maintainer of the artifact is not a software engineer, or the artifact's purpose is a throwaway demo/prototype for stakeholder communication.
non_engineer_surface.binary_test: Will a non-engineer edit this artifact after the engineer leaves?
non_engineer_surface.measurement: Named maintainer is a non-engineer, or artifact is explicitly labeled demo with an expiry date. Otherwise FALSE.
non_engineer_surface.true_example: Operations lead tweaks a visual assistant flow weekly.
non_engineer_surface.false_example: Engineer-built internal tool that happens to have a UI.

evidence_schema.expiry_date: 'YYYY-MM-DD' or null — engineer maintainer WITHOUT an expiry date is CONTRADICTED (that is an internal tool; rerun selection without the claim)

non_engineer_surface.hard_boundary: Verdict is Flowise and durable_admissible=false. It can never be promoted to durable; a durable rewrite is a new build under a new selection.

multi_agent_graph.definition: The workflow is a graph of >=3 cooperating agents where control flow backtracks (retries a node, revisits a stage, or dynamically chooses the next node based on intermediate output), or requires LangSmith-grade distributed tracing, or needs Deep Agents-style context compression across agent handoffs.
multi_agent_graph.binary_test: Is there a cycle in the agent graph, a dynamic router node, or a cross-agent tracing/compression requirement?
multi_agent_graph.measurement: Draw the agent graph. No cycle AND no dynamic router AND no distributed-tracing requirement = FALSE.
multi_agent_graph.true_example: Research loop: planner -> three parallel workers -> critic -> replan (cycle on critic verdict).
multi_agent_graph.false_example: Linear summarize-then-post pipeline — that is a chain, use Pydantic AI.

evidence_schema.graph_shape: one of cycle | dynamic_router | distributed_tracing | context_compression
evidence_schema.agent_count: integer >= 3 — fewer is CONTRADICTED (a linear chain is not a graph)

agent_reasoning.definition: Producing the output requires interpreting unstructured input or exercising judgment that cannot be expressed as a fixed transformation of the inputs; a human would have to read and decide.
agent_reasoning.binary_test: Could a deterministic function with full access to the same inputs produce acceptable output?
agent_reasoning.measurement: Write the deterministic alternative in one sentence. If it exists and meets the quality bar, the property is FALSE and the MODEL op fails necessity.
agent_reasoning.true_example: Read an inbound email and decide if it is a buying signal.
agent_reasoning.false_example: Extract fields from a fixed-format webhook payload — that is parsing.

evidence_schema.unstructured_input: string, non-empty — what must be interpreted
evidence_schema.deterministic_alternative: string, non-empty — the alternative that was considered
evidence_schema.alternative_rejected_because: string, non-empty — the falsifiable reason it cannot meet the bar

default.definition: None of the above properties holds: a scheduled or triggered job whose logic is deterministic code plus at most typed model calls in validated slots.
default.binary_test: All five properties above answered FALSE.
default.measurement: Kestra flow wrapping Pydantic AI agents is the correct verdict.
default.true_example: Nightly scraper -> typed agent summary -> CRM write.
default.evidence_schema: none — default is the absence of claims

kestra_pydantic.when: Default for every scheduled or event-triggered job.
kestra_pydantic.where: Kestra flows in the rig namespace; agent code as Python scripts under an authority root.
kestra_pydantic.how: Trigger -> Shell/Python task -> Pydantic AI agent (typed I/O) -> structured result -> store/alert. Flow YAML is the single orchestration source of truth.
kestra_pydantic.prohibited: Business logic in flow YAML templates; model calls outside typed pydantic boundaries; secrets in flow variables.
kestra_pydantic.d85_obligations: Flow YAML + agent source under authority root; MODEL ops carry typed schemas + necessity; four ratios >= 0.85.
kestra_pydantic.migration: Landing target for all launchd periodic scripts and Flowise flows that outgrow prototype status.

temporal.when: clock_critical only: a start-latency SLA <= 60s with mandatory catch-up.
temporal.where: Temporal namespace rig; workflows as code in the temporal worker repo.
temporal.how: Workflow as Python/Go code; activities call Pydantic AI agents; retries/timeouts/schedules declared in workflow code, never in agent prompts.
temporal.prohibited: Using Temporal for convenience scheduling; cron-with-jitter requirements (that is Kestra); describing Temporal as a wall-clock guarantee.
temporal.d85_obligations: Workflow code under authority root; every activity typed; four ratios >= 0.85; deployment evidence (measured start latency + recovery time) meeting the declared SLA.
temporal.migration: Existing 4 schedules audited against the evidence schema: any without a <=60s SLA and catch-up policy move to Kestra.

orca_pydantic.when: agent_reasoning: the job IS an agent making decisions in a workspace.
orca_pydantic.where: Orca worktree automations with Pydantic AI I/O contracts.
orca_pydantic.how: Orca automation declares typed input/output models; agent reasons inside; deterministic guardrails bound every outward action (Gate-D).
orca_pydantic.prohibited: Scripts that do not reason (move to Kestra); untyped free-text agent outputs; agent-decided scheduling/retries.
orca_pydantic.d85_obligations: Choosing Orca declares MODEL ops: necessity records required at admission; control plane stays CODE.
orca_pydantic.migration: 3 of 11 existing automations identified as non-reasoning scripts: move to Kestra.

langchain.when: multi_agent_graph: cycles, dynamic routing, LangSmith tracing, or Deep Agents context compression.
langchain.where: langgraph projects under an authority root with pinned dependencies.
langchain.how: Graph as code; nodes are typed callables; state is a pydantic model; conditional edges are deterministic functions of state.
langchain.prohibited: Linear chains (use Pydantic AI); provider switching as the justification; prompt strings as the routing mechanism.
langchain.d85_obligations: Graph definition under authority root; every node typed; necessity records for MODEL nodes; four ratios >= 0.85.
langchain.migration: None existing; new builds only when the graph test passes.

flowise.when: non_engineer_surface: non-engineer builder or explicit demo/prototype.
flowise.where: Flowise canvas; export JSON kept in the prototype archive with an expiry date.
flowise.how: Visual build; documented owner; expiry review date; no production credentials.
flowise.prohibited: Durable operation; production secrets; promotion by editing — a durable rewrite is a NEW selection under kestra_pydantic/orca_pydantic.
flowise.d85_obligations: durable_admissible=false, permanently. Cannot pass closed-grammar inventory; cannot be scheduled as a durable system.
flowise.migration: Any Flowise flow needed in production is rebuilt, not exported.

launchd.where: ~/Library/LaunchAgents plists, one plist per service, KeepAlive semantics declared.
launchd.how: plist declares sockets/watch paths; service binary is Python under an authority root; internal scheduling is still code.
launchd.prohibited: StartCalendarInterval/StartInterval jobs (that is Kestra territory); resident daemons that merely poll a schedule.
launchd.d85_obligations: plist + source under authority root; plist is control plane and therefore CODE; four ratios >= 0.85.
launchd.migration: 64 launchd periodic jobs move to Kestra; ~50 true residents stay.

4_temporal_schedules.audit: any that tolerate >60s drift move to Kestra

11_orca_automations.action: keep 8 agent-driven, move 3 scripts to Kestra

64_launchd_periodic.superseded_by: authority/standards/estate_ledger.v1.json mechanical scan: 149 periodic move candidates; counts here were user-table estimates

build_checklist: build declares process_id and the inventory_sha256 snapshot it was generated against; certification recomputes the live inventory and only binds when the declared process matches the target AND the declared hash equals the live hash (stale or mismatched checklists are CHECKLIST_BLOCK, never rebound)
framework matches select_framework() output for the declared properties
flowise verdicts are prototypes; no durable system declares flowise
every MODEL op has typed pydantic input/output schemas
every MODEL op has a D85 necessity record
an archify diagram showing how the process works is present and parses
orchestration (schedule, retry, timeout, cancellation, dispatch) is code, never model-decided

what_good_looks_like.selection: the framework is the output of the decision table for declared properties, decided before the first line of logic is written
what_good_looks_like.typing: every model boundary crosses a pydantic model in both directions; nothing accepts or returns free text across a boundary
what_good_looks_like.necessity: every MODEL op carries a falsifiable claim, a deterministic alternative, and reachable CODE fallbacks
what_good_looks_like.orchestration: a human reading only the Kestra/Temporal/plist config can predict when the job runs, what it retries, and when it gives up
what_good_looks_like.diagram: an archify artifact exists that a non-author can follow from trigger to terminal state without reading the source
what_good_looks_like.admission: the process has passed inventory -> classification -> REALIZED_PASS scoring, and outward effects have a dormant Gate-D arm

changelog.change: Rolled back the keepalive_daemon resource kind: KeepAlive proves restart policy, not a held resource, and admitting it would certify the current estate by definition. Residents require plist resource evidence or OS-corroborated listeners; KeepAlive-only jobs land in needs_review. Estate counts superseded by the mechanical scan in estate_ledger.v1.json.

Checklist schema now requires process_id and inventory_sha256. Enforcement certification (certify_build / checklist subcommand) is claim-and-verify: the build declares the snapshot digest it was generated against, certification recomputes the live inventory, and binding happens only on exact equality. Declared/target process mismatch, stale hash replay, and unbound runs are each typed CHECKLIST_BLOCK paths. A direct check_build_checklist() PASS is self-described inventory_binding=unbound and is not an enforcement verdict.

Verdict binding is enforceable end to end: certification attaches checklist_sha256 (canonical digest over the full closed-schema build), and a consumer-side verifier (verify_certification / verify-cert subcommand) recomputes the digest, rejects non-exact certificate schemas, rejects unbound or non-PASS certificates, and blocks post-cert mutation replays, tampered snapshot hashes, and live-inventory drift. A saved PASS paired with a mutated build now BLOCKs at the boundary that consumes it.
